title: Siegard survey material
description: The frontmatter of one file of material read from source no delivery wrote — «The first material of an adopted system is read from its source alone, stating observable behavior, each fact beside the path it was read at» (SPEC-005 R2). The body carries six headings, in this order: `## Facts`, `## Answers`, `## Vocabularies`, `## Upstream artifacts`, `## Outside the domain`, `## Observed and not decided here`. A fact line is a top-level bullet (`- `) under the first four headings, ending with the path it was read at in backticks; an indented bullet belongs to the fact above it. `bin/trace.py --ledger` reads the fact lines to hold a ledger to the material, and the paths on them to say which files each candidate node is read against. A heading with nothing to say carries the line `None.`.

contract_version.description: Which contract this material was written against.

target.description: The key of `siegard.json`'s `targets` the paths below are spelled from.

files.description: Every file the survey read as its area, spelled from the target source root. The adoption's file set is this list, and a fact line names a file of it.

read_outside_area.description: Any other file opened to understand one of the area's, with why, one line each. Read, never surveyed: no fact is attributed to it.
